verdict: PARTIAL -- epistasis is real (46%) and predictable held-out (r=0.45), BUT almost all of it is the GENERIC SATURATION nonlinearity (additive-only control r=0.45; pair-specific gain only -0.001). So combinatorial data reveals a predictable nonlinearity, but little PAIR-SPECIFIC transmission -- the responsiveness-prior story repeating one level up. A real but limited win.
note: Combinatorial (double-perturbation) test of what would break the far-field wall, on Norman&Weissman 2019 K562 (scPerturb). Epistasis = double response - additive(sum of singles) = the buffering/transmission signal single-KO endpoints cannot see. Reports how non-additive doubles are and whether per-gene epistasis is predictable for HELD-OUT pairs (GroupKFold). Directly tests whether the data KIND the wall_diagnosis learning curve pointed to actually recovers the missing coefficient.
